 Rosales, Laure deliver knockout blows as Choco Mucho storms into semis
 Sisi Rosales set the stage, and Eya Laure brought down the curtains.
 Powered by their vaunted 1-2 punch, the two Choco Mucho stars delivered when it mattered most, fending off a spirited PLDT fightback to fashion out a 25-22, 25-23, 18-25, 25-23 victory and secure the Flying Titans' place in the semifinals of the PVL All-Filipino Conference Siklab Series at the SM Mall of Asia Arena in Pasay late Thursday night.
 With a precious Final Four berth on the line, both teams came out determined to keep their championship dreams alive. But in a match marked by fierce exchanges and momentum swings, Choco Mucho proved the steadier side, holding its ground under pressure before unleashing its finishing punch in the fourth set.
 Rosales was virtually unstoppable, soaring above the PLDT defense and pounding in crucial points to keep the Flying Titans ahead as the High Speed Hitters mounted a determined comeback. Then came Laure, who came off the bench in the stretch and delivered the knockout blows, scoring Choco Mucho's final three points to slam the door on PLDT's rally.
 Her final strike was a fitting exclamation point – a thunderous attack that zipped past top libero Kath Arado before the ball kissed the floor and bounced out of bounds, leaving PLDT with no answer and Choco Mucho erupting in celebration.
 The Flying Titans celebrated as though they had won the championship. In many ways, however, the victory carried that kind of weight, sending them into the Final Four with a 5-3 record at the end of the elimination round and joining unbeaten Nxled (7-0) and Farm Fresh (5-2) in the semifinal cast.
 For PLDT, the defeat left its Final Four hopes hanging by a thread. The High Speed Hitters finished with a 4-4 mark and now need a favorable combination of results to keep their campaign alive.
 PLDT's slim mathematical chance hinges first on Creamline losing its final elimination-round assignment against Farm Fresh on Saturday. The High Speed Hitters must then prevail in the FIVB points tiebreak to claim the remaining semis berth.
 But Choco Mucho had little reason to dwell on the permutations. It had seized its opportunity, and Rosales made sure her team would not let it slip away.
 Still breathless after finishing with 21 points, including the crucial hits down the stretch, Rosales revealed the personal resolve that fueled her performance, saying she had promised herself and her husband that she would leave everything on the court.
 “Pagdating ko rito, sinabi ko sa sarili ko at sa asawa ko na kahit mapagod ako nang husto, basta maibigay ko lang ang lahat,” she said. “Sinabihan ko rin ang mga teammates ko na atin na ito. Huwag na nating pakawalan.”
 Rosales had earlier expressed her desire to keep training even after the elimination round. With Choco Mucho now through to the semis, that determination takes on greater significance as the Flying Titans shift their sights toward a bigger prize.
 Beyond her own performance, Rosales was quick to acknowledge the collective effort that carried the team through, crediting her teammates for staying together and executing the game plan. She also reserved heartfelt thanks for the Choco Mucho faithful, whose unwavering support never wavered through the team's ups and downs.
 “Sobrang thankful ako dahil kumapit at nagtiwala ang lahat ng teammates ko, at nagawa rin namin ang game plan,” she said. “Maraming salamat din sa fans na mula day one, anuman ang mangyari sa team, nandiyan lang palagi sa likod namin.”
 For Choco Mucho, the victory was more than a ticket to the semifinals. It was a statement of composure, character and championship resolve – with Rosales leading the charge and Laure delivering the final word in the two-hour showdown.
 Laure finished with 11 points, but Choco Mucho drew contributions from several other heroes, as Maddie Madayag added seven markers, Jewel Encarnacion chipped in six, including a strong second-set showing, while Caitlin Viray and Isa Molde contributed five points apiece.
 Their collective effort gave the Flying Titans a 65-59 advantage in attack points, more than making up for their 2-11 deficit in blocks. PLDT dominated at the net but failed to provide the wing support needed by Savi Davison.
 The Fil-Canadian ace erupted for 30 points, along with 10 excellent digs and 22 receptions, but her production slowed in the fourth set as her fellow High Speed Hitters struggled to step up. Dell Palomata led PLDT's blocking effort with five kill blocks and finished with nine points, while Jessa Ordiales and Alleiah Malaluan contributed seven apiece. Mika Reyes added six points, Jovie Prado had four, while Kim Dy was limited to just three. 
 Deanna Wong also had the edge in playmaking, tallying 11 excellent sets while sharing setting duties with Alina Bicar. The duo outperformed PLDT's Kim Fajardo, who recorded nine excellent sets, and Angge Alcantara.
 Thang Ponce and Dawn Catindig likewise anchored Choco Mucho's floor defense, with Ponce recording 13 digs and Catindig contributing 12 receptions and 13 digs.
